rfc3339Utc.description: RFC 3339 instant in UTC. Local offsets are rejected so that canonical serialization cannot depend on a local time zone (Section VI-C).

evaluationBasis.description: Section V: closed set. A GC-IR condition never evaluates a probability directly.

onUnknown.description: Section V: every context condition declares on_unknown. For mandatory gates on_unknown = fail is required, not default.

reasonCode.description: Closed at schema v1.0 (Section V), extended at v1.1 (Section III), extended at v1.2 (Paper 2 v1.2 spec section 1L). RC-01 no per-action observable; RC-02 no authority-matrix action; RC-03 requires probabilistic judgment; RC-04 (v1.2) discrete action is gateable but the profile-required timing assurance has not been established, compile-ineligible; RC-05 consequence class undefined; RC-06 (v1.1) continuous control, fails AD-1, belongs to the runtime safety layer. RC-04 and RC-06 are deliberately distinct control-layer defects (see gcir.rc_routing): RC-06 is the wrong layer entirely (route to standing safety/RTA), RC-04 is the right layer with missing timing assurance (compile-ineligible, never auto-routed to RTA).

warningCode.description: WC-01 unresolved obligation reference. A warning, never a disposition.

requirementClass.description: Schema v1.1 adds 'standards' (a consensus standard -- ISO, IEC, ASTM -- applied by the profile).

enforcementPhase.description: Schema v1.1. Only PRE_AUTHORIZATION and BOUNDARY_REVALIDATION contribute to the PERMIT aggregate. A predicate declaring no enforcement_phase is treated as PRE_AUTHORIZATION (v1.0 backward compatibility).

evaluationLatencyBound.description: Schema v1.1, Section III AD-2. The bound within which the evaluator must signal completion; expiry is on_evaluation_timeout = HOLD, never a partial permit.

onEvaluationTimeout.description: Schema v1.1. Fixed, not configurable: an evaluator that does not finish inside evaluation_latency_bound resolves to HOLD.

stateBinding.description: Schema v1.1, Section IV-C / VIII (INV-STATE-BINDING). The world-state attribute tuple a permit issued under this predicate is digested over; a mismatch between the digest at authorization and at the execution boundary is HOLD by default, forcing re-authorization -- never a silent permit.

mismatch_response.description: The signed policy's declared fail-closed response to a digest mismatch. HOLD (forcing re-authorization) unless the approved specification explicitly and signedly declares DENY instead; never a silent permit either way.

concurrencePolicy.description: Schema v1.1, Section IV-C / V commitment 7. All-or-nothing N-of-M; partial concurrence never accrues. expiry_response is fixed DENY.

delegationRef.description: Schema v1.1, Section V commitment 7. Names the delegation relationship a predicate over the DELEGATE transition participates in; strict containment of the issued child permit against its parent is checked at issuance by auxiliary check A3, not by the compiler (the compiler never sees a parent permit instance).

responsePolicy.description: Schema v1.1, Section VII-I. Governs whether a conformant runtime must emit a HumanResponse record for permits issued under this predicate.

primaryClass.description: Schema v1.2, Paper 2 v1.2 spec section 1B. Every derived artifact (compiled predicate) has exactly one primary class; a requirement may produce several artifacts, each with its own single class. Prohibited class collapse (e.g. human -> auth, meta -> auth) is rejected by gcir.contract_v12.primary_class_preservation, not by this schema alone.

interpretationStatus.description: Schema v1.2, Paper 2 v1.2 spec section 1F. An ACS or invariant declaring 'unresolved' on a mandatory semantic interpretation that would compile into an active (runtime) control is COMPILE-FAIL / release-inadmissible (gcir.validation.constraint_18_no_unresolved_mandatory_interpretation), never a runtime DENY or HOLD.

exceptionRef.description: Schema v1.2, Paper 2 v1.2 spec section 1G. Every declared exception preserves its target requirement, trigger, authorized actor(s), parameter bounds, scope, and lifecycle/version binding. A scope of '*'/'ALL'/'GLOBAL' or an empty scope is a global bypass and is rejected by gcir.contract_v12.exception_scope, not permitted merely by this schema.

synchronizationContract.description: Schema v1.2, Paper 2 v1.2 spec section 1J. Validates representation of the synchronization contract only (gcir.contract_v12.synchronization_contract_representation); it does not prove runtime synchronization.

observationObligation.description: Schema v1.2, Paper 2 v1.2 spec section 1K. Omega_r = (beta_r, kappa_r, q_r): beta_r is the required binding information, kappa_r the observation obligation's own declared content, q_r the required observation scope.

declaredPathRef.description: Schema v1.2, Paper 2 v1.2 spec section 1I. The declared in-scope path id this predicate is the gate/placement mapping for; validated by gcir.contract_v12.declared_path, which checks only the DECLARED path set, never complete mediation.

consequenceDescriptor.description: c_i = (kind_i, materiality_i, reversibility_i, authority_i) -- Section VII-A.

reversibility.description: Schema v1.1 adds 'requires_intervention' (Section VII: physical_harm_to_person is reversibility-qualified over {irreversible, requires_intervention}).
